$schema_note: LaunchReel journey eval set. Each case is a real YC Summer-2026 company. This file doubles as the pre-render hero set for the Buildathon-TV / 'we already made your launch trailer' stunt. Difficulty 'hero' = strong marketing site, safe to pre-render and show off; 'hard' = extraction-hostile site that stress-tests Scout. Source: https://yc-oss.github.io/api/batches/summer-2026.json (92 companies, verified live 2026-07-12). fetch_signals were captured with a plain curl -L (no JS render) on 2026-07-12 and are the evidence behind difficulty.

selection_policy.hero_rule: Recognizable-ish name + visually strong marketing site that loaded 200 with rich content (large HTML, many , og:image). These are the ones we pre-render for the TV stunt and DM first.
selection_policy.hard_rule: Loads 200 but is extraction-hostile in a distinct way (near-empty page / JS-only SPA with no static imagery / image-heavy non-root homepage). These prove the pipeline degrades gracefully, not that it looks good.
selection_policy.excluded_on_purpose: Isengard Industries (AI munitions, 8.6MB image-heavy) and Greypoint Industries (autonomous swarm warfare, 2.6KB sparse) technically fit hard-mode signals but were excluded: seeding a promotional launch-trailer pipeline — and the public YC-S26 TV gallery — with military-strike marketing content is out of scope for this stunt. Molagri, Coasty and Rise Reforming exercise the same three extraction failure modes without that.

cases.name: screenpipe
cases.one_liner: Capture how you work and turn that into agents

fetch_signals.title: screenpipe: Workflow Memory for AI Agents

cases.why_selected: Most recognizable name in the batch — popular open-source project with a real developer following, so a founder seeing 'we already made your trailer' lands. Dense, polished marketing site (282KB, 94 images, og:image) gives Scout a strong logo, hero shots and real product UI to pull from. Dev-tool dark aesthetic diversifies the palette spread across the hero set.
expected_challenges: Product-heavy site with real terminal/desktop UI screenshots — Real-UI truthfulness matters: Product Tour scenes must use the actual captured screenshots, not a hallucinated dashboard.
Likely dark theme; brand-fidelity check must confirm the trailer honors a dark palette rather than defaulting to a light template.

cases.name: Palette
cases.one_liner: An interactive AI video generation and editing platform

fetch_signals.title: Palette — The creative engine for video

cases.why_selected: On-the-nose demo case: Palette is itself an AI video-generation platform, so a LaunchReel trailer for a video company is the sharpest possible show-of-strength on the TV wall. Clean, colorful, design-forward site (107KB, 22 images) is the visual opposite of screenpipe and stresses brand-color fidelity.
expected_challenges: Meta risk: a video-gen company will judge motion quality and eases the hardest — this is the case to hold to a 5 on Motion quality.
Colorful brand system; palette extraction must capture the accent(s) accurately or the brand-fidelity gap is obvious.

cases.name: Definite

fetch_signals.title: Definite | Cut bank reporting time and cost

cases.why_selected: Fintech/data product with dashboard and metric-dense product screenshots (380KB, 37 images) — the ideal case to exercise Product Tour A/B, metric counters, and the Real-UI truthfulness dimension (numbers and chart labels must be legible and true to the real UI).
expected_challenges: Financial metrics on screen — any hallucinated or smeared number is an auto-fail on both text legibility and real-UI truthfulness.
Clean but restrained palette; brand fidelity is about typography and neutral tones, not a loud accent.

cases.name: Rex
cases.one_liner: AI Operations Partner for Enterprise Order to Cash

fetch_signals.title: Rex | The AI operations partner for order-to-cash

cases.why_selected: Polished enterprise-B2B marketing site (445KB, 47 images, og:image) with product UI and a clear value narrative — a straightforward 'this should look great' hero that tests whether the default pipeline produces a shippable enterprise-credible trailer.
expected_challenges: Enterprise tone: VO/script must read credible-and-calm, not hypey — VO/audio-sync and tone are the risk here, not visuals.
Order-to-cash is abstract; Problem and Product Tour scenes must make a back-office workflow legible without inventing UI.

cases.name: Context.dev
cases.one_liner: We give AI agents realtime web context.

fetch_signals.title: Context.dev: Web Scraping & Crawl API for AI Agents

cases.why_selected: Richest page in the hero set (733KB, 68 images) and a clean developer-infrastructure brand — good for testing that Scout doesn't drown in a large page and still extracts the right logo, accent, and hero copy. Recognizable-ish in the AI-agent tooling scene.
expected_challenges: Very large page — Scout's fetch/brief step must not truncate to boilerplate nav/footer and must find the real hero message.
Developer-API product with little consumer imagery; Product Tour scenes lean on code/API visuals that must render legibly (auto-fail if code text smears).

cases.name: Molagri
cases.one_liner: Biopesticides that are safe for humans and bees.
cases.why_selected: Failure mode: near-empty homepage. 1.6KB of HTML, zero tags — effectively a stealth splash page. Scout has almost nothing to extract beyond the tagline and og:image, so this proves the pipeline degrades gracefully (falls back to YC one-liner + logo + generated brand-locked b-roll) instead of producing garbage.
expected_challenges: No real product UI exists — Product Tour scenes have nothing truthful to show; the correct behavior is abstract brand b-roll + concept framing, NOT a hallucinated dashboard (this case tests that the pipeline refuses to fake UI).
Only inputs are the one-liner, the YC logo, and an og:image; brand palette must be inferred from minimal signal.
Agriculture/biotech, not SaaS — the SaaS-motion templates must adapt or the trailer feels off-genre.

cases.name: Coasty
cases.one_liner: The computer-use agent that doesn't break on real software. We will…

fetch_signals.title: Coasty - #1 Computer-Use AI Agent
fetch_signals.notes: Large page but 0 static — JS-rendered SPA; final URL resolved to coasty.ai:443; YC one_liner is itself truncated ('We will…').

cases.why_selected: Failure mode: JS-only SPA + malformed upstream metadata. 499KB of HTML but zero static images means a plain fetch sees no logo or hero shots — Scout MUST use the Cloudflare Browser Rendering screenshot path (renderJs) or it gets nothing. The YC one_liner arrives truncated ('We will…') and the site resolves via a quirky http→:443 redirect, so it also tests robustness to dirty inputs.
expected_challenges: Static fetch yields no imagery — if the screenshot step is skipped or fails, brand fidelity and real-UI truthfulness both collapse; this is the case that validates the Cloudflare screenshot dependency.
Truncated one_liner from YC ('We will…') — the script/CTA must not print the ellipsis fragment verbatim; Scout's brief has to reconstruct a clean value prop.
http:// + :443 redirect quirk — intake URL normalization must not choke.

cases.name: Rise Reforming
cases.one_liner: We turn waste gases into valuable supply-secure chemicals

fetch_signals.title: Home | Rise Reforming
fetch_signals.notes: Homepage lives at /home, not the domain root; 2MB page dominated by large images/video.

cases.why_selected: Failure mode: image-heavy, non-root homepage, hard-to-visualize domain. 2MB page whose content is mostly big photos of industrial equipment, and the real homepage is at /home rather than the bare domain. Tests that Scout follows to the actual homepage, doesn't blow its token/asset budget on 2MB of imagery, and can make climate-chemistry (a physically un-glamorous B2B-hardware domain) look like a launch.
expected_challenges: Homepage is /home not / — if intake normalizes to the bare domain it may hit a thinner page; URL handling must preserve the path or discover the real homepage.
Heavy hero photography of plants/reactors, little UI — Product Tour scenes must lean on real photos/process diagrams, not a fake SaaS dashboard.
Chemical-process brand with muted industrial palette — motion and music must sell 'hard-tech credibility', a different register than the consumer-SaaS default.
